data.narrative: Shipped a consistent, safe error envelope plus structured request-correlated logging. The DECIDE choice was graceful degradation (B) for runtime availability - the public redirect hot path must never 500 when a cache or queue is down - while input validation stays fail-fast. The BREAK surfaced a hole in that resilience layer: the unhandled-exception handler leaked raw exception text into the 500 body, which I reproduced, root-caused to passing str(exc) into the envelope, and fixed by restoring the static safe message with redaction kept on log context, closing with a full regression run (35 passed).

dimension_scores.observation: Chose graceful degradation for external dependencies (cache/queue down -> fall back to Postgres, log degradation, never 500 the redirect) while keeping validation fail-fast; named the exact hot path that must not degrade.
dimension_scores.evidence: module_05 decision B reasoning recorded: 'the public redirect hot path must never 500 because a cache or queue is down - fall back to the source of truth (Postgres) and log the degradation'.

dimension_scores.observation: Reproduced the injected stack-trace leak via the failing regression test (assert 'boom' not in response body), root-caused it to unhandled_exception_handler passing str(exc) as the message, fixed the one-line bug, and closed with the full suite green.
dimension_scores.evidence: test_unhandled_error_returns_safe_500 failed during BREAK ('boom' contained in 500 body) then passed after the fix; pytest -q: 35 passed.

dimension_scores.observation: Kept the redaction contract intact: raw exception text and bearer tokens never reach responses or logs; the sentinel DO_NOT_LOG_ME_123 is asserted absent from responses and redact('password=supersecret')==='password=[REDACTED]'.
dimension_scores.evidence: test_errors.py secret-not-logged + redact helper tests pass; unhandled handler logs error=redact(str(exc)) and returns only 'internal server error'.

dimension_scores.observation: Every 4xx/5xx carries a stable error.code, human message, and request_id for support correlation; request middleware logs request_id/method/path/status/duration_ms so incidents can be replayed from logs alone; 4xx/5xx split and no-trace rule applied uniformly.
dimension_scores.evidence: app/main.py access_log middleware + HTTPException/validation/unhandled handlers; test suite covers 400/401/404/429/500 envelopes all carrying request_id.

dimension_scores.observation: Documented the error contract (code/message/request_id), the redaction rules, and the BREAK-FIX root cause with exact status-code proof in the Module 05 evidence file.
dimension_scores.evidence: progress/evidence/module-05/evidence.txt records the envelope shape, 4xx/5xx mapping, and the reproduced leak + fix.

strengths: Root-caused the stack-trace leak to the exact line (str(exc) passed into error_envelope) instead of wrapping or masking the symptom.
Kept the fail-closed contract: 500 bodies never contain exception internals, sentinel never leaks, redaction verified by regression tests.
Closed the loop with a full regression run (35 passed) after the one-line fix.
data.recommendation: Next module: put Redis in front of the redirect hot path with explicit invalidation on write - the graceful-degradation fallback you chose means cache-down must never surface as a 500, so the read-through path needs a test that proves it.

public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the app gives clients a stable error contract and gives operators correlation IDs - the foundation for incident debugging in production.

public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates a production instinct - the difference between a safe 500 and a leaky one is exactly what separates demo code from shippable services.
